abstract: Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case. As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian Čech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.

title: TernScope: Model-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient Ternary Endoscopic Segmentation
authors: Zhuoyu Wu, Wenhui Ou, Qiawei Zheng, Xuhong Qiu, Wenqi Fang, Raphaël C. -W. Phan
abstract: Edge medical segmentation must reconcile small model size, high accuracy, and fast inference. TernScope addresses this tradeoff through model--hardware co-design, learning a compact segmentation network whose low-bit operators also simplify hardware execution. Split-channel large-kernel blocks preserve spatial context with limited computation, while branch fusion removes redundant inference paths. Ternary Progressive Quantization-aware Training (TPQ) then adapts the fused network from deep to shallow layers, through the decoder, and finally to the input and prediction layers. All 25 convolutions use ternary weights and 8-bit activations, enabling packed storage and multiplier-free computation. The resulting model uses 0.2483 M parameters and 0.0949 GMACs while retaining competitive segmentation accuracy on in-domain and external datasets. Under the same 45 nm technology, TernScope reduces compute-array area by 88.46% compared with the original Gemmini, a systolic-array accelerator with 8-bit $\times$ 8-bit multipliers. These results demonstrate a path from accurate lightweight medical segmentation to compact low-bit hardware.

title: Diff-IrisPAD: Modeling Bona Fide Iris Distributions for Unsupervised Presentation Attack Detection
authors: Geetanjali Sharma, Harsh Yadav, Tanmay Deshpande, Shubham Ashwani, Aditya Nigam, Raghavendra Ramachandra
abstract: Iris recognition systems are vulnerable to presentation attacks (PAs), including textured contact lenses, print replays, and synthetic irises. Existing PAD methods rely on supervised learning with attack data, limiting generalization to unseen attacks and new sensors. We propose Diff-IrisPAD, an unsupervised framework based on Brownian Bridge Diffusion that models bona fide iris distributions without using attack samples. The method reconstructs clean iris textures from degraded inputs and detects attacks via reconstruction inconsistency using ViT scoring and pixel-level measures. Experiments on a large-scale multi-sensor dataset (125K+ images, NIR and VIS, 8 attack types) show that Diff-IrisPAD achieves an overall ACER of 30.52, significantly outperforming diffusion-based baselines while demonstrating strong generalization to unseen attacks. These results highlight the effectiveness of diffusion-based bona fide modeling for robust and scalable iris PAD.

title: Overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1: Patient-Specific Phenotype Concept Recognition in Full-Text Biomedical Literature
authors: Xuanlyu Zhu, Feng Tian, Yang Zhong, Pengqi Zheng, Xiwen Bi, Ling Luo, Yuanyuan Sun, Jian Wang, Lingfei Lin
abstract: Automatic phenotype information extraction plays an important role in rare disease diagnosis, genotype-phenotype analysis, and precision medicine. However, accurately identifying phenotype concepts and determining their associations with specific patients remain challenging, particularly in full-text biomedical articles involving multiple patients and complex clinical descriptions. This paper presents an overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1, which aims to promote the development of methods for patient-specific phenotype concept recognition from full-text biomedical literature. The task consists of two subtasks: full-text phenotype concept recognition and patient-specific phenotype association. For this evaluation, we used 200 annotated full-text biomedical articles from the PatientPheX dataset, containing 506 patients, 15,193 phenotype mentions, and 5,656 patient-phenotype associations. A total of 455 teams registered for the competition, with 189 and 103 valid submissions received on the Phase A and Phase B leaderboards, respectively. The best-performing system achieved an overall score of 0.7389 on the final test set, outperforming the baseline by 8.37 percentage points. The top-performing teams explored diverse approaches combining biomedical language models, large language models (LLMs), and ensemble strategies. The evaluation results highlight both the potential of these approaches and the remaining challenges in patient attribution and phenotype normalization from full-text biomedical literature. The post-evaluation phase remains open at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/competition/entrance/532512.

title: Accurate Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization calculations with Gaussian basis set
authors: V. K. Ivanov, D. A. Glazov, A. V. Volotka
abstract: We apply a large Gaussian basis set of size up to $N = 500$ to calculate the all-order Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization correction in highly-charged ion. For a hydrogen-like system, this allows us to obtain an accurate correction value with a level of precision comparable to that of traditional methods. We demonstrate that values of effects that can be calculated as the difference between two quantities, such as the nuclear model correction, converge faster than the absolute value of the correction. We discuss the basis extrapolation methods and show their use in estimating the error due to incomplete convergence. Finally, we show an application of the Gaussian basis set to calculation of the vacuum polarization screening correction in lithium-like ions.

title: Demand Estimation for Rationally Inattentive Consumers
authors: Ruolei Zhu
abstract: We develop a rational-inattention BLP (RI-BLP) model for demand estimation from aggregate market shares, allowing for endogenous prices and unobserved preference heterogeneity. We establish conditions for uniqueness of market-share inversion and construct a simulated RI-BLP GMM estimator with instrumental-variable moments and market-share constraints. Under regularity and simulation-accuracy conditions, the estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal as the number of markets grows, with the number of products fixed. Monte Carlo experiments show accurate recovery of mean utility coefficients, with less precise estimates of dispersion parameters. In a canned-tuna application, RI-BLP and logit yield similar average own-price elasticities. Unlike logit, the fitted RI-BLP model implies that a price increase can reduce demand even for similar products and shift demand toward the outside option.

title: Sharp Moser-Onofri inequality on the CR sphere under zero-moment constraints and its application to the stability of the CR Moser-Onofri inequality
authors: Lu Chen, Guozhen Lu
abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. By combining a decomposition into low and high spherical harmonics with the known CR localization estimates, we first prove the existence of extremals of the subcritical Moser--Onofri inequality under zero-moment constraints. We then derive their Euler--Lagrange equation, establish their smoothness, and eliminate the moment multiplier by means of the infinitesimal CR conformal action. Using the summation identity (4.9) on the Hardy space $H^2(B^n)$, we show that the extremals of subcritical Moser-Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints are constants. By a limiting argument, we deduce the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. As an application, we establish the stability of Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere with the best stability constant.

title: Integral trace forms of cyclic number fields without tameness
authors: Zhi-Lin Zhang
abstract: Let $K/\mathbf{Q}$ be a cyclic number field and let $T_K=\bigl(\mathcal{O}_K,(x,y)\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbf{Q}}(xy)\bigr)$ be its integral trace lattice. We prove that two cyclic number fields have isometric integral trace lattices if and only if they have the same degree, signature, and signed discriminant. More generally, an isomorphism between the Dirichlet character groups of two finite abelian extensions that preserves the conductor and parity of every character yields an isometry of their integral trace lattices, equivariant for the dual identification of Galois groups. For cyclic fields, the degree, signature, and discriminant determine the character group together with these two functions. This proves Bolaños's conjecture for wildly ramified cyclic fields and gives the corresponding extension of the tame classification: in general, the signature must be retained as an additional invariant.

title: Coherent differentiation with a monoid of degrees: derivatives, Taylor expansion, finite differences...
authors: Thomas Ehrhard, Aymeric Walch
abstract: Coherent differentiation has been introduced a few years ago as a refinement of the (categorical semantics of the) differential lambda-calculus and of differential linear logic, compatible with the determinism of computation, and hence in categories where addition of morphisms in the hom-sets is only partially defined. In this setting differentiation is implemented by a kind of ''tangent functor'', with the difference that it maps an object to its object of summable tuples rather to a tangent bundle. In our earlier work, these tuples were pairs in the case of simple differentiation, and families indexed by integers when dealing with Taylor expansion and the Fa{à} di Bruno formula. We push this idea further, considering now tuples indexed by an arbitrary commutative partial monoid satisfying a nonnegativity condition. The monoid structure on these indices plays a crucial role in the definition of the ''differential'' calculus associated with this ''tangent functor''. In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.

title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
authors: Junhyeok Park, Jungeun Yoon, Kyungmin Kim, Hunsoon Lee, Shinyoung Ahn, Kangho Kim
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. To address this, we propose HAWK, a transfer mechanism that enables rapid KV cache transfer across heterogeneous devices. HAWK establishes a remote direct memory access (RDMA) path for direct cross-device transfers while handling inter-device tensor layout discrepancies as part of the transfer process. In particular, HAWK allocates tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side to match the target tensor layout. Leveraging these buffers, HAWK orchestrates data transfer from a conventional contiguous GPU RDMA buffer to the corresponding NPU buffers, allowing transferred tensors to be consumed directly without additional data rearrangement while maintaining transfer efficiency. We implement and evaluate HAWK on a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, demonstrating performance within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26$\times$ higher power efficiency and 1.72$\times$ higher cost efficiency.

title: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
authors: Viral Patel, Boyin Tan, Jason Xue, Youcheng Sun
abstract: Coding agents can invest substantial effort in repository exploration and testing yet still produce unsuccessful patches. Existing online steering methods review trajectories periodically or invoke an advisor when a monitor detects behavioral problems; frequent reviews are costly, and the absence of anomalous behavior does not mean that an agent is on the right track. We propose PAUSE, a framework for steering coding agents with a single planning intervention. Agents reach their first source-code edit at a median of 60% of trajectory progress, after exploration, bug reproduction, and testing. PAUSE intercepts this edit request before it executes, which requires no learned monitor, no search over checkpoints, and no extra model call (search-free). A separate Planner reads the task and the pre-edit transcript and writes one repair plan; the same agent, the Executor, resumes with this plan, keeping its context and workspace. PAUSE applies online, during a live run, and offline, from a recorded trajectory prefix. We evaluate PAUSE on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual with two Executors and three agent harnesses. With Qwen3-coder as Executor and GPT-5.6 Sol as Planner, online steering improves resolution by 16.8% on Verified in OpenHands and by 14.7% on Multilingual in SWE-agent. In SWE-agent, PAUSE outperforms LivePlan, a rule-triggered advisor, by 3.2% on Verified and 3.7% on Multilingual at similar Planner cost, and is comparable to SICA's periodic overseer at about 11-15% of its Planner cost. Offline, PAUSE recovers 35.4% of eligible failed Verified tasks, and resuming from the recorded prefix uses 33-41% fewer Executor tokens than restarting.

title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
authors: Wyatt James Horne
abstract: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.

title: Regularity and $v$-number of syzygies of graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules
authors: Samarendra Sahoo
abstract: Let $A=Q/(\mathbf f)$, where $Q$ is a polynomial ring over an infinite field $k$ and $\mathbf f=f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is a homogeneous $Q$-regular sequence. For $1\leq j\leq c$, set $w_j=\operatorname{deg}(f_j)>0.$ Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded $A$-module of infinite projective dimension. Set $M_i=\operatorname{Syz}_i^A(M)$. We prove that, for each $l\in\{0,1\}$, the sets $\operatorname{Ass}_A(M_{2i+l})$ eventually stabilize, and that $\operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$ is eventually bounded above and below by linear polynomials. If $w_j=w$ for all $1\leq j\leq c$, then the functions $i\longmapsto \operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$, $i\longmapsto v(M_{2i+l}),$ and $i\longmapsto v_{\mathfrak p}(M_{2i+l}),\, \mathfrak p\in\mathcal A_l,$ are eventually linear with leading coefficient $w$, where $\mathcal A_l$ denotes the stable set of associated primes.

title: Automated Discovery of Physically Interpretable Subgrid Length Scales for Detached Eddy Simulation via Agentic AI
authors: Jiawei Chen, Xiang I. A. Yang, Ping He
abstract: Traditional turbulence-model development relies heavily on expert knowledge and is time-consuming. This study develops an agentic AI framework, DEScover (automated Discovery of DES closures), to explore subgrid length scales for detached eddy simulation (DES). The user provides only a modeling idea: the length scale is the grid width normal to the local vortex axis. Four large language model (LLM) agents then propose, review, implement, and evaluate candidate formulations and generate scripts for CFD simulations. The Discovery Agent infers the vortex axis from various vortex-identification methods. The candidates are tested on four cases spanning canonical and engineering flows: a flat plate, a backward-facing step, a free shear layer, and an iced airfoil. For all test cases, the best candidate consistently outperforms the standard length scale based on the maximum cell size. Its accuracy is similar to, or slightly better than, that of the expert-designed shear-layer-adapted length scale. Each agentic discovery run takes about 25 minutes on average, excluding the CFD simulations. These results show that LLM-based reasoning can significantly accelerate the discovery of physically interpretable turbulence models and reduce reliance on manual expert formulation.

title: Memory Manipulation
authors: Benson Tsz Kin Leung
abstract: We study persuasion that works through memory: a manipulator alters the probabilities with which a Bayesian decision-maker recalls the signals he has received. The decision-maker corrects for the elevated or reduced probabilities of recalling different signals, and this correction disciplines what manipulation can achieve. Manipulation cannot move the average posterior. It backfires on decision-makers with few memories, whose sparse recall is evidence against the favored state, yet it is effective on those with many, who can be led to arbitrarily confident beliefs in the wrong state. It thickens the right tail of the belief distribution and, under Poisson memory, lowers its hazard rate. In a monopoly pricing application, the seller manipulates memory retrieval at high prices, and manipulation in turn raises the optimal price. In a narrative persuasion application, memory manipulation reduces information provision and creates echo chambers.

title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
authors: Zhi Li, Guoxin Wei, Cheng Xing
abstract: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.

title: AT-Differ: Dataset for Audio-Text Difference Captioning
authors: Akihiro Fujii, Yuki Okamoto, Yuki Saito, Hiroshi Saruwatari
abstract: Evaluating audio-text semantic alignment is important in various audio-language tasks. Existing methods mainly quantify audio-text semantic alignment using a single score and cannot explicitly describe how audio and text differ. In this paper, we propose audio-text difference captioning, a task that generates textual descriptions of differences between audio and text. We also construct a new dataset AT-DIFFER containing audio-text pairs with systematically simulated differences and corresponding difference captions. Using AT-DIFFER, we fine-tune an existing multimodal large language model to describe differences between audio and text. The experimental results show that the original model has limited ability to describe such differences, whereas fine-tuning on AT-DIFFER substantially improves this ability.

title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
authors: Zedong Peng
abstract: Agent memory systems such as Mem0 and Zep decide what to keep before any question arrives; coding agents keep the raw history and let the model search it with its own tools. We ask whether designed memory still helps once the model is strong enough to search for itself. On one LoCoMo conversation (419 turns, 152 questions), we run four memory methods (full context, BM25, Mem0, Zep) and three coding agents (Pi, Codex, Claude Code), each with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5, and record what every rollout costs. This is a short empirical study, with one conversation and one run per cell. Agent memory is a costly patch for a weak model: Mem0 beats full context only with GPT-4o-mini, and its build alone costs more than a whole full-context rollout. Agent memory also has a ceiling, set by the model that writes it: a stronger reader does not recover what a weaker writer left out. With Claude Opus 5.5, Pi tops the cost-accuracy frontier, scoring 99% for less than half the cost of full context; its one miss is a wrong answer key. Part of that lead comes from photo captions that only the agents could read: on the 88 questions whose evidence has no photo, Pi and full context differ by one answer.

title: Controlling Variability in~Neuroimaging Analysis Pipelines with~Software Product Lines
authors: Gauthier Le Bartz Lyan, Paul Temple, Boris Clenet, Mathieu Acher
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties. In this document, we advocate for the conceptual adoption of SPL principles as a promising direction to improve reproducibility and consistency in neuroimaging research.

title: NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction
authors: Julian Silva, Jaliya Kodithuwakku, Navindu Sirimanna, Shaveen Herath, Wageesha N. Manamperi, Joshua P. Kulasingham
abstract: Driven by recent advancements in hearing assistive devices, target speaker extraction (TSE) in multi-talker environments has drawn significant attention. To address this, hearing technologies identify attention using neural signals recorded via electroencephalography (EEG) to guide TSE, enabling neuro-steered auditory attention decoding. However, most existing techniques rely on time-frequency masking, which suffers from low fidelity in spectro-temporally overlapping regions and is often restricted to narrowband audio. In contrast, we introduce NeuroCodec, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first generative EEG-guided TSE framework operating in the latent space of a neural audio codec. Specifically, NeuroCodec models spatial EEG dependencies via graph convolutions and fuses cross-modal EEG and speech representations through attention mechanisms and Mamba-based temporal modeling. We further introduce a six-phase training curriculum that progressively incorporates latent reconstruction, multi-scale spectral, and adversarial objectives to ensure stable, high-fidelity speech generation. Experiments on the public Cocktail Party and KUL datasets show NeuroCodec outperforms baselines, across several perceptual metrics. A listening experiment with 20 participants validated that NeuroCodec offers greater perceptual accuracy, achieving a mean score of 82.24 compared with 49.63 for M3ANet. Additionally, the proposed method is seen to enable 44.1 kHz reconstruction with spectral content extending up to 20 kHz, further supporting the perceptual results. Finally, we extend NeuroCodec with a causal streaming formulation suited for real-time processing, providing a basis for hearing assistive devices.

title: Strong Positive Recurrence for Strongly Entropy Expanding Maps
authors: Alexandre Delplanque, Hengyi Li
abstract: We introduce expanding strong positive recurrence (expanding-SPR) for non-invertible systems with critical points. We then give a sufficient condition for maps to be SPR: strong entropy expansion (SEE). We prove that expanding-SPR implies good thermodynamical properties, including exponential decay of correlations of Hölder observables for the measures of maximal entropy. The class of maps that are SEE includes all C^{\infty}-interval maps with h_{top}(f )>0 and all Viana maps.

title: Prefix Visibility Ratio: Quantifying Partial Observability in Carpet Bombing Detection
authors: Farid Naït-Abdesselam, Laaziz Lahlou, Doha Bentaoussy, Hugo Lege, Eve Lin, Nadjia Kara
abstract: Carpet bombing attacks distribute malicious traffic across many destinations within a network prefix, while operational monitoring commonly provides destination-specific telemetry for only a subset of those targets. This creates an attack-conditional observability problem that is not captured by address utilization or nominal monitoring coverage. We introduce the Prefix Visibility Ratio (PVR), defined as the fraction of attacked destinations for which the telemetry required by the host-level evidence plane is available, and argue that PVR should be treated as an explicit evaluation dimension for carpet bombing detection. We then present VANTA (Visibility-Aware Network Threat Analysis) as one concrete way to operationalize this principle. VANTA combines host-level and prefix-level anomaly scores, estimates PVR online from router-side destination evidence and the monitored-destination inventory, and adjusts evidence fusion according to both estimated visibility and estimator confidence. Across a validated campaign of 2,160 Mininet runs, VANTA achieves 99.18% precision, 93.46% recall, a global F1-score of 96.24%, and a 1.54% false-positive rate. In a separate matched-observability study using task-adapted feature-level reference implementations, VANTA reaches 95.89% pooled F1 and 92.39% recall for configured PVR<=10%, with its largest advantage appearing at configured PVR=1%. These reference comparisons are intended to isolate observability effects under a common binary detection task rather than to reproduce the original end-to-end objectives of the referenced systems. The results establish attacked-destination visibility as a measurable factor that can materially change detector behavior and should be reported explicitly in future carpet bombing evaluations.

title: B$_{4/2}$ anomaly related to the shape coexistence in $^{94}$Zr
authors: P. Buganu, R. Benjedi
abstract: Solutions of the Bohr-Mottelson Hamiltonian with a sixth-order anharmonic oscillator potential, for both axially-symmetric and $γ$-unstable deformations, are applied to investigate the lowest states of the $^{94}$Zr nucleus. The experimentally observed $B_{4/2}$ anomaly is explained, within the present approach, by the presence of a coexistence between an approximately spherical shape ($2_{1}^{+}$) and an axially-symmetric deformed one ($4_{1}^{+}$). On the other hand, the energies of the $0_{2}^{+}$ and $2_{2}^{+}$ states and their associated electromagnetic transitions fit better a dynamical triaxial deformation configuration ($γ$-unstable). This overall picture of the lowest states in $^{94}$Zr corresponds to a triple shape coexistence scenario.

title: Fixed geodesics of involutions on $3$-spheres
authors: Bin Shen, Hui Zhang
abstract: Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2π$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.

title: Solutions of $x^α+y^α=1$ in $λ$-Cantor sets
authors: Kan Jiang, Nero Ziyu Li, Lifeng Xi
abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^α+y^α=1$ with both coordinates in a $λ$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $α>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. To explore the structure of the solutions, for arbitrary $α$, we find that their Hausdorff dimension undergoes phase transitions as $λ$ varies: we establish the occurrence of Hausdorff phase transitions by proving the existence of zero-dimensional and positive-dimensional regions.

title: Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI?
authors: Benaya Trabelsi, Jonathan Shaki, Sarit Kraus
abstract: Asked what to study, which career to pursue, or what product to build, large language models (LLMs) often recommend AI-related options. We ask where this tendency comes from by comparing models before and after fine-tuning and by varying how questions are asked. First, pretrained models already include explicit AI/ML terms in the recommendations of 27% of their responses, and their released instruction-tuned versions do so in 59%. Second, fine-tuning models ourselves shows that this rise is not inevitable: general instruction tuning leaves the rate unchanged, but removing the 7% of instruction examples that concern AI cuts it by 14 percentage points, below the level of the pretrained models it starts from. Data rewarding helpfulness raise it by 9 points, while data ranked by the preferences of diverse simulated users lower it by 9. Finally, with models held fixed, asking for the "best" option or for what to do "right now" raises the rate by 8 and 18 points, whereas telling the model it is an AI advisor adds 4. Overall, the tendency starts in pretraining, and what models learn afterward, together with how a question is phrased, decides how strongly it appears.

title: Observation of Size-dependent Optical Modes and Confinement in Fin Cavities using Angle-Resolved Cathodoluminescence
authors: Kiana Malmir, Jonathan Lee, Douglas Cameron, Babak Nikoobakht
abstract: We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. FDTD also reveals a transition from multi-mode to single-longitudinal-mode behavior in 200-nm fins, consistent with experimentally observed fringe narrowing. Increasing fin length from 10 μm to 30 μm compresses fringe spacing via longer round-trip paths. Conversely, tilting the fin end-facet from 90° to 45° reduces the effective light path length, increasing the incoherent optical emission. Remarkably, this loss can be offset by adjusting the fin length-to-height ratio. Results suggest WARCL is a robust in-situ method for direct characterization of individual dielectric nanocavities, mapping their modal profiles and light directionality as a function of geometry for custom design of nanoscale optical sources and waveguides.

title: Do Flow-Generation Tools Matter? Unsupervised Characterization of MQTT Traffic Across Public Datasets
authors: Mohammed Rashed, Carlos García-Rubio, Celeste Campo
abstract: Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) is widely used in IoT environments due to its lightweight publish-subscribe design and suitability for resource-constrained networks. While current MQTT security studies mainly focus on detecting attacks and optimizing classification performance, this work takes a different perspective by presenting a cross-dataset, tool-aware characterization of MQTT traffic at the flow level. This perspective is motivated by the fact that flow-generation is tool-dependent: flows are not directly observed in packet captures, but are constructed through tool-specific decisions about packet grouping, flow termination, and feature export. Using packet captures from 4 public MQTT datasets, we generated over 380K flows with 3 open-access flow-generation tools: Zeek-flowmeter, Argus, and NTLFlowLyzer. We analyzed the tool-specific flows using K-means, DBSCAN, and HDBSCAN, with and without PCA-based dimensionality reduction. We measured clustering quality using 2 metrics: (1) Silhouette score to assess label-independent cluster compactness and separation, and (2) Adjusted Rand Index to measure agreement with available labels. Our results show that the choice of flow-generation tool affects the resulting flow population, feature-space structure, and clustering behavior. Zeek-flowmeter achieves the best performance in several settings, particularly with K-means and PCA reduction to 10 components. Yet, no single tool consistently dominates across all datasets, algorithms, and evaluation metrics. These findings show that flow-level MQTT analysis should treat the dataset, flow-generation tool, preprocessing choices, clustering algorithm, and evaluation metric as interconnected experimental factors.

title: Encoding a bosonic mode into qubits for simulating boson-matter interactions
authors: Maarten Stroeks, Jelena Mackeprang, Yaroslav Herasymenko, Barbara Terhal
abstract: We explore the space-time cost of encoding of a bosonic mode into a set of qubits via various encodings, and their resilience to noise. In particular, we compare the performance of the unary Fock state encoding, an unexplored encoding of Fock states into Dicke states (``Dicke'' encoding), and the binary quadrature encoding. We do so by considering a displacement as well as a simulation of a Dicke model, coupling a bosonic mode to a set of atoms represented as qubits. Using classical simulations, we assess the accuracy and optimized space-time costs in terms of number of qubits, circuit depth and CNOT count of a quantum simulation of the time dynamics using these encodings. Although our study is far from comprehensive, we find that the binary quadrature encoding is overall most favorable in terms of being very space-efficient and relatively time-efficient due to the use of the quantum Fourier transform. Our novel Dicke encoding leads to very shallow circuits, but pays in terms of using many more qubits. We probe the use of an H2-2 Quantinuum trapped-ion qubit device (56 qubits) for displacement and Dicke model simulation in the low boson-number regime, where we find that noise leads to visible deviations from ideal circuit dynamics.

title: Fast2Peak: High-Fidelity Restoration Algorithm by Single-Pixel Masking towards Real-Time Spectral Measurements
authors: Nan-Nan Zhang, Si-Heng Luo, Xin-Di Pei, Wen-Xuan Li, Jun Wang, Yi-Fan Bao, Hao Ma, Guo-Kun Liu, Bin Ren
abstract: Improving the temporal and spatial resolution of spectroscopy inevitably reduces the photons available to each measurement, pushing rapid measurements into photon-starved conditions where weak spectral features are obscured by stochastic background noise. Here, we present Fast2Peak (F2P), a self-supervised Transformer framework that transforms the spectral restoration task into a context-prediction problem. Given that physically constrained spectral signals exhibit strong local continuity, whereas the stochastic noise fluctuates randomly and does not possess the continuity across neighboring spectral pixels, single-pixel masking enables F2P to restore the predictable signal structure while suppressing unpredictable fluctuations even without clean reference spectra. Unlike conventional offline spectral restoration, F2P achieves high-fidelity restoration within milliseconds, enabling real-time "acquire-and-process" operation. We demonstrate this capability in time-resolved electrochemical SERS and hyperspectral Raman imaging, where spectral restoration is performed during data acquisition. In addition, F2P has demonstrated its robust generalization across different instruments and spectral modalities, including Raman, NMR, XRD and FTIR.

title: Bridging Foundational and Agentic Capabilities of LLMs
authors: Wei Guo, Yuanjian Xu, Jianing Hao, Yongyao Duan, Ran Chen, Zhong Li, Guang Zhang
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents, yet it remains unclear how their foundational capabilities translate into agentic capabilities. End-to-end scores leave unresolved whether low benchmark capability or weak deployment drives a failure, limiting actionable diagnosis. We bridge foundational and agentic capabilities through an operation-level measurement framework. We represent each model with a foundational profile derived from capability benchmarks and an operation profile derived from interaction trajectories, and define capability realization gaps as deviations of observed operation performance from predictions based on foundational capabilities. Experiments on fifteen model services in $τ^2$-Bench show that foundational profiles only partially predict agentic operations. Models with comparable profiles can differ substantially in execution, and these gaps remain consistent across task subsets. Operation profiles add information and substantially improve task-score prediction. The framework locates execution departures at the operation level to inform model development and agent evaluation. We will release our code and analysis artifacts.

title: LEAF-Mamba: Feature Adaptation and Fusion for Whole Slide Image Analysis
authors: Lubin Gan, Jing Zhang, Mingjun Ma, Linhao Qu, Dachun Kai, Xiaoyan Sun
abstract: Whole slide image (WSI) analysis enables computational diagnosis and prognosis, but gigapixel images and limited annotations make slide-level learning challenging. Multiple instance learning addresses this task by aggregating patch representations from frozen pretrained encoders. Recently, Mamba has enabled efficient modeling of long patch sequences. However, task supervision alone does not explicitly constrain information recovery during feature adaptation, while Mamba couples local processing with long-range propagation rather than retaining separate representations for fusion. Motivated by these challenges, we introduce LEAF-Mamba, a framework that jointly addresses latent evidence adaptation and fusion for frozen-feature WSI analysis. A reconstruction-regularized adapter learns compact, task-specific representations while reconstructing the input features. Parallel Mamba and convolutional streams then capture long-range dependencies and sequence-local interactions, with an input-dependent gate modulating their joint representation before slide-level pooling. Experiments across feature extractors demonstrate improved average performance over strong MIL baselines in both diagnostic classification and survival prediction. Component analyses further support the contributions of adaptation and fusion. These findings highlight the value of jointly designing feature transformation and contextual aggregation to translate pretrained representations into effective slide-level predictions.

title: On Almost MDS codes holding $(n-k-1)$-designs and an open problem on Witt design
authors: Huakai Wei, Shiyuan Qiang, Shaofang Hong
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an almost maximum distance separable (AMDS) code over the finite fields with parameters $[n,k,n-k]$ whose minimum-weight codewords support an $(n-k-1)$-$(n,n-k,λ)$ design. We first determine the parameters of the dual code $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. We also characterize the design and its complementary design supported by the minimum weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. In particular, we present explicit formulas for the weight enumerators of all subset codes of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$ with length at least $k+1$. These formulas are completely determined by the cardinality of the subset, the dimension, together with the parameter $λ$, and are independent of the specific choice of subsets. As an application, we answer an open problem posed by Wang, Tang and Ding in 2023 by proving that the $3$-design supported by the minimum-weight codewords in their proposed cyclic dual code is isomorphic to the complementary design of the Witt spherical geometry design.

title: APED-CXR: Adaptive Privileged Evidence Distillation for Chest X-Ray Grounding with Image-Only Inference
authors: Md Shihabul Islam Shovo, Nishi Kanta Paul, Jamil Fayyad
abstract: Compact chest X-ray (CXR) models that localize findings suit deployment, but box annotations are limited and report-aware multimodal models are expensive at inference. We introduce APED-CXR, which distills report-informed spatial evidence from a frozen multimodal teacher into a student with 11.1M parameters that predicts diseases and boxes from shared evidence maps and requires the image alone at test time. During training, the teacher uses the radiograph, report, and queried class to evaluate regions proposed from the student's current evidence maps, and its support scores serve as training targets for the student's pooled evidence scores within these regions. Trained on PadChest and evaluated on held-out PadChest-GR, refreshing the student's proposals for teacher evaluation improves box-level localization F1 from 0.302 with fixed warm-up proposals to 0.338 (IoU >= 0.5; gain 0.036, 95% CI [0.022, 0.049]), while maintaining diagnostic AUC. This gain depends on the teacher checking current proposals: with equally many random boxes, a fixed dense box set, teacher-generated boxes, or report rules instead of the teacher, F1 stays near the fixed-proposal level, and proposals two refreshes old recover only part of the gain. On NIH ChestX-ray14, a secondary test set, box recall also rises from 0.423 to 0.447.

title: Coronal spectroscopy - Past, Present and Future
authors: Jagdev Singh, R. Ramesh, V. Muthu Priyal
abstract: After the beginning of photography of solar corona during the eclipses in the year 1860, efforts began to carry out spectroscopic observations of solar corona. During the total solar eclipse of 1868 August 18 at Guntur, Madras state, the observation of emission line 5875Å by Janssen lead to the discovery of Helium. Next year, during the eclipse of 1869 August 7, Charles Young and William Harkness discovered green emission line around 5310Å (later measured as 5303Å). It was interpreted as due to Coronium, an unknown element. The identification of this green line in 1939 due to [Fe xiv] ion showed the corona to be hot at 10^6 K. High resolution spectroscopic observations indicated that width of emission lines to be more than expected. The excess line width was interpreted in terms of existence of non-thermal velocity. Recent spectroscopic observations have indicated a complex nature of variation of emission line parameters with height above the corona. The spectroscopy of solar corona is also performed in other wavelengths, such as UV, EUV, X-rays, visible, infrared, and radio part of the spectrum. Here, we discuss the past spectroscopic observations of solar corona, present observations with various instruments, such as Visible Emission Line Coronagraph onboard Aditya-L1, and need for the spectroscopic observations in future.

title: Bio-Inspired Auditory Processing: Coupling Parallel Resonate-and-Fire Dynamics with Ternary Recurrent Networks for Speech Recognition
authors: Pavlos Poulos, Katelyn Sadorf, Themos Stafylakis, Costas A. Anastassiou
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient inference through sparse, event-driven computation, yet remain constrained on continuous, context-dependent tasks such as automatic speech recognition (ASR). A key bottleneck is the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, whose membrane decay erases information across pauses and phonetic boundaries while it must both extract features and retain long-range context. Inspired by cortical separation of nonlinear filtering and somatic integration, we introduce the Spiking Ternary GRU (stGRU): a ternary-weight gated recurrent unit performs temporal filtering, while downstream Resonate-and-Fire (RF) neurons generate the binary spike stream driving the next block's event pathway. This makes binary event transmission a native training constraint rather than a separate deployment-time activation quantization step; together with ternary weights, learned projections avoid dense floating-point matrix MACs. Trained end-to-end on LibriSpeech-960, Small, Medium, and Large stGRUs reach 8.09%, 7.04%, and $6.44 \pm 0.17\%$ WER on test-clean without an external language model. To our knowledge, these are the first matrix-MAC-free spiking networks without a learned ANN sequence decoder to achieve single-digit WER on LibriSpeech. The architecture also achieves 10.88% test CER on Aishell-1 (9.28% on dev) when trained from scratch. Internally, trained networks develop a depth-graded hierarchy: shallow layers act as fast acoustic filters, while deep layers form slower semantic integrators whose latent representations segregate into part-of-speech manifolds and word-level spike events. Deep-layer firing rates follow lognormal distributions with a sparsity gradient, mirroring hierarchical processing observed in human cortex in vivo. Our biologically grounded architecture combines competitive ASR with favorable modeled compute and memory cost.

title: Kinetic Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation in collisionless plasmas: a correlated noise source
authors: Fabio Moretti, Oreste Pezzi, Simone Benella, Giuseppe Consolini, Andrea Larosa, Fabio Lepreti, Luca Sorriso-Valvo, Francesco Valentini, Vincenzo Carbone
abstract: We here focus on small-scale dynamics of collisionless plasmas by employing a generalized kinetic Langevin framework driven by a stochastic time-correlated forcing. Our investigation captures the steady-state Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation (FDR) where the energy injection at low frequencies is due to the time-correlated forcing and the small-scale energy conversion occurs via Landau damping, the latter --though formally reversible-- acting as an effective dissipation mechanism. We analytically extract the resulting asymptotic spectral scalings across multiple physical regimes and characterize the velocity-space cascade by decomposing the plasma distribution function with Hermite polynomials. The framework is then generalized to a multi-scale forcing scenario in which correlation rates are distributed according to a power-law distribution. This extension provides closed-form analytical expressions that may serve to interpret spacecraft in-situ observations. All analytical predictions are successfully validated through direct numerical integrations of the underlying kinetic equations.

title: Spin order and excitations in the collinear kagome antiferromagnet Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$
authors: Jin Ding, Yang Liu, Feihao Pan, Yinghao Zhu, Yixi Su, Stanislav E. Nikitin, Ursula B. Hansen, Mechthild Enderle, Zhilun Lu, Linxuan Song, Yong-Chang Lau, Xiaoyan Ma, Enke Liu, Huiqian Luo
abstract: Kagome lattices host rich magnetic, topological, and transport phenomena owing to their geometric frustration and strong spin correlations. Here we present a systematic neutron scattering study of the kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$, which orders into a collinear $c$-axis antiferromagnetic (AF) state below $T_N =$ 551 K. An additional anomalous Hall effect (AHE) contribution beyond the conventional magnetization-scaling response is observed well below $T_N$ under an in-plane magnetic field $\mathbf{B} \parallel ab$. Elastic neutron scattering demonstrates that the Fe moments preserve their collinear $c$-axis AF alignment down to 1.5 K at zero field. Inelastic neutron scattering reveals a distinctive Y-shape spin excitation dispersion exhibiting a two-gap structure below 10 meV, likely arising from two nondegenerate spin-wave branches. Polarized neutron measurements further show that the low-temperature spin excitations are strongly anisotropic: the in-plane component $M_{ab}$ dominates while the $c$-axis component $M_c$ is nearly absent. Upon warming, $M_c$ gradually grows markedly but remains much weaker than $M_{ab}$ even at 300 K. We propose that the unconventional AHE originates from a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting either in the static or dynamic configurations due to gapless excitations. These findings establish the collinear AF kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$ as a platform for chirality-driven AHE without spontaneous spin reorientation.

title: Stellar Loci X: Selection of Nitrogen-Rich Giants Using GALEX NUV and Synthetic SDSS Photometry
authors: Liangyu Yu, Haibo Yuan, Baitian Tang, Kai Xiao, Xue Lu, José G. Fernández-Trincado
abstract: Nitrogen-rich (N-rich) field stars (likely second-generation escapees from globular clusters) provide a powerful, but currently sample-limited, probe of globular-cluster disruption in the Galactic halo. We exploit the fact that enhanced NH, CN absorption depresses optical u band flux, while the near-ultraviolet (NUV) band is largely insensitive to nitrogen enhancement while remaining sensitive to overall metallicity. Combining GALEX NUV photometry with (synthetic) SDSS optical photometry, we construct a [Fe/H]-dependent stellar-locus model for giants and select significant redder u-g outliers as N-rich candidates. For a relaxed cut ([Fe/H] <= -0.8, 2 sigma) we identify 970 candidates, with an estimated completeness of 64-65% and purity of 41-62% from multiple validations. A stricter selection ([Fe/H] <= -1.0, 3 sigma) yields 220 candidates, with lower completeness (30-38%) but substantially higher purity (60-91%). The dominant contaminants show anomalous spectral energy distributions (e.g., UV excess), and are themselves useful targets for follow-up. The diverse kinematic and dynamical properties of our candidates suggest multiple origins. This scalable photometric approach enables systematic searches for N-rich halo stars and is well suited to forthcoming wide-field surveys such as CSST.

title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
authors: Zakaria Fattah, Ilias Ftouhi, Giorgio Saracco
abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.

title: Benchmarking Coding Agents for System-Level Performance Optimization
authors: Yanze Zhang, Maggie Yongqi Guan, Shudong Liu, Qi Hao, Kanye Ye Wang, Meng Qu, Xiaobo Zhou
abstract: Coding agents are becoming an increasingly important paradigm for automating software engineering tasks. However, existing coding benchmarks primarily evaluate agents at the function or repository level, leaving their capabilities in more complex distributed software systems largely unexplored. In practice, many modern applications adopt microservice architectures, where end-to-end performance emerges from interactions among multiple independently running services, requiring agents to reason beyond local code changes. To study this capability, we introduce MicroPerf-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents on end-to-end performance optimization in microservice systems. Constructing such a benchmark is challenging because reproducible system-level performance fixes are sparse and difficult to attribute. We address this challenge by injecting empirically grounded performance anti-patterns into real-world open-source systems while preserving functionality and ensuring measurable performance degradation. The resulting benchmark contains 65 optimization instances across seven systems and nine anti-patterns, each with an executable environment, functional tests, and mixed-workload evaluation. Across 1,755 runs covering nine agent-model configurations, the best configuration recovers only 42.0% of the injected performance degradation. The dominant failure is not invalid code, but functionally correct and constraint-compliant changes that fail to improve end-to-end performance, highlighting system-level bottleneck localization as a key challenge for current coding agents. The source code and data are available at https://github.com/zyzcjnb/microperf.

title: Efficient Generative Image Compression with Quantized Latents Refinement
authors: Hao Cao, Yinhuan Huang, Wenqi Guo, Zhijin Qin, Jungong Han
abstract: Generative image compression (GIC) delivers strong perceptual quality at low bitrates. However, GIC methods with strong perceptual quality often rely on pretrained diffusion models with high latency, while recent lightweight GIC methods reduce latency but deliver lower perceptual quality. We observe that, for lightweight GIC methods at low bitrates, coarse deterministic quantization can collapse nearby encoder latents corresponding to different fine details to the same point, making these details difficult to recover. Motivated by this, we propose GR-GIC, an efficient GIC that delivers competitive reconstruction performance with fast inference. For better performance, we introduce Guided Refinement (GR), which combines latent refinement guided by entropy context with adaptive perturbations for training regularization, jointly improving reconstruction at low bitrates. For fast inference, we introduce reorganized projected residual vector quantization (P-RVQ), which equivalently reorganizes residual updates into low-dimensional lookups to expose greater parallelism and reduce sequential computation. Experiments on Kodak show that for performance, compared with OneDC, GR-GIC achieves BD-rate savings of 23.19%, 37.71%, 22.30%, and 22.14% for LPIPS, DISTS, PSNR, and FID, respectively. For fast inference, the highly optimized implementation of GR-GIC encodes and decodes in 4.60 and 5.98 ms on an NVIDIA A100. Specifically, the reorganized P-RVQ implementation achieves a $3.14\times$ average speedup over the original implementation under the same FP32 setting. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, GR-GIC achieves latency comparable to lightweight GIC methods.

title: Optimally Emulating Smooth Functions for Bayesian Analyses
authors: Scott Pratt, Oleh Savchuk, Eren Erdogan, Ekaksh Kataria, Christal Martin, Syed Afrid Jahan, Frederi Viens
abstract: For Bayesian analyses aimed at constraining the parameter space of computationally expensive models by comparison with heterogeneous data sets, model emulators play a pivotal role. Model emulators enable searches through high-dimensional parameter spaces, searches which might otherwise require millions of full model runs. Here, an emulation strategy is presented based on the assumption that the model output can be well described by a polynomial expansion with all terms being independent of one another and with higher order terms being given decreasing weights according to a convergence parameter. It is found that if the expansion's form is constrained to being invariant to rotation and translation of the parameter space that the polynomial form becomes equivalent to that of a Gaussian process emulator using a correlation kernel with a Gaussian form. In the limit that the function is smooth, quantified by a convergence parameter, $Λ$, it is found that rather few training points are required to reproduce the full model and provide a good estimate of its uncertainty. An accuracy metric is defined based on an average of the expected uncertainty over the prior before training data are actually gathered. Analytic expressions for the expected accuracy are provided based solely on an expected value of $Λ$ and the location of the training points. This enables a tenable optimized placement of training points, which is shown to be significantly superior to random placement or that from Latin hyper-cube sampling. Examples of optimized placement are provided, and the accuracy is studied as a function of various variables, such as the number of model parameters, the number of training points, and the convergence parameter.

title: Lifting PCA in the Wasserstein Space
authors: Jérémie Bigot, Clément Bonet
abstract: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a fundamental tool for statistical dimension reduction, yet no canonical extension to distribution-valued data has emerged within the framework of optimal transport. While Wasserstein barycenters and Wasserstein least-squares regression provide canonical liftings of Euclidean averaging and linear regression in the Wasserstein space, an analogous principle for PCA has remained unexplored. In this paper, we introduce Lifted PCA, a canonical extension of Euclidean PCA to Wasserstein space, obtained through the framework of lifting functionals in the space of probability measures by convex extension. Starting from the classical variational formulations of PCA on the Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds, we derive two equivalent minimization problems over probability measures supported on these manifolds that correspond to Wasserstein barycenters with generalized costs. We establish an exact analogue of the equivalence between the Stiefel and Grassmann formulations of Euclidean PCA, preserving PCA's original variational structure under lifting. We further derive dual formulations and optimality conditions, and establish equivalences with multimarginal optimal transport and matching-for-teams problems. We also establish statistical consistency for empirical estimators and develop computational algorithms based on the Wasserstein barycenter formulation over the Stiefel manifold. Whereas Euclidean PCA summarizes vectors through projections onto an optimal low-dimensional linear subspace, Lifted PCA summarizes probability distributions through an optimal probability measure supported on multiple low-dimensional subspaces. Numerical experiments on distributional datasets illustrate the practical performance of the proposed methodology and its benefits for distributional data analysis.

title: Learning to Reason Like a Cytopathologist:Clinically Grounded Multiscale Evidential Learning for Cervical Cytology
authors: Ajeet Kumar Singh, Nehal Mishra, Anurag Tripathi, Santanu Chaudhury, Dorien Herremans
abstract: Cervical cytology presents a fundamentally ambiguous diagnostic landscape, where equivocal categories such as Atypical Squamous Cells of Undetermined Significance (ASC-US) occupy a morphological grey zone that is definitional. For clinical decision support, the goal extends beyond assigning a definitive label to every sample: cases must also be distinguished by whether the available evidence supports a confident decision or warrants further consideration, a distinction conventional classification models are not designed to explicitly represent. We propose a multiscale evidential framework that models cervical cytology along an ordinal disease continuum using clinically grounded soft anchors, representing progression from benign reactive changes to precancerous lesions and malignancy. Three biologically motivated spatial contexts--nuclear morphology, cytoplasmic characteristics, and neighbourhood cellular architecture--are independently encoded using a shared frozen DINOv2 backbone, preserving inter-scale disagreement that early fusion may obscure. Calibrated predictions are transformed into Dempster--Shafer belief masses and fused with reliability discounting, allowing conflicting evidence and insufficient support to remain explicitly uncommitted rather than forcing a decision. The fused belief state drives interpretable routing that separates confidently classified cases from those with irreducible evidential insufficiency, enabling clinically meaningful triage. Across two independent publicly available conventional cytology datasets, RIVA and CRIC Cervix, the framework generalises consistently, with uncertainty strongly associated with diagnostic difficulty: incorrect predictions carry 1.94x-4.13x higher uncertainty than correct ones.

title: Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining
authors: Xintong Liu, Chenkai Zhang, Yanzhao Ma, Peng Yang
abstract: Formulaic alpha factor mining searches for symbolic expressions that transform market data into predictive signals. Recent LLM-based evolutionary factor mining methods use large language models as semantic variation operators. Under the conventional LLM-EA paradigm, stochastic variation and fitness-based selection can leave the search weakly directed and concentrated around a narrow set of structurally similar factors. We argue that these limitations arise because current methods mainly organize search at the individual and population levels, leaving lineage-level control underused. A lineage connects successive factor variants through evolutionary descent. We propose LineageEvo, which uses lineage in two coupled forms of search control: (1) lineage-conditioned LLM variation, which distills Lineage-Scoped Search Experience into operator-specific priors and fuses them with global operator priors, providing persistent, lineage-relevant guidance for LLM generation; and (2) lineage-stratified search allocation, which balances factor quality against lineage concentration by distributing the search budget across lineages during evolutionary search. Together, these mechanisms make semantic variation more direction aware and prevent branches from dominating the evolution, thereby promoting the discovery of predictive and diverse factors. We evaluate LineageEvo on CSI 500 and S&P 500 in terms of factor predictiveness, portfolio performance, search efficiency, and lineage- and expression-level diversity. LineageEvo achieves the strongest predictive performance on both markets, while LSPS produces a more balanced lineage distribution and a structurally broader factor pool. The results support lineage as a useful intermediate unit for controlling LLM-based evolutionary factor search.

title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
authors: Kuniko Paxton, Ifeoluwa Wuraola, Dhavalkumar Thakker
abstract: The deployment of small and quantized language models in resource-constrained settings raises an important fairness question: when a compressed model produces fewer biased responses, does this reflect fairer behavior or greater abstention? We study this problem in Question Answering (QA) using the BBQ benchmark across multiple model sizes and quantization settings from Qwen3, Gemma-3, and SmolLM2. We also examine whether the observed trends remain stable across alternative prompt formulations and when the ``Unknown'' option is removed in a forced-choice setting. Our results show that larger models achieved higher QA accuracy, but bias showed no simple scaling trend and quantization effects varied across configurations. Notably, 20 of the 26 configurations with fewer biased responses also show increased over-abstention, indicating that lower observed bias can partly reflect greater abstention. These findings show that lower observed bias can partly reflect greater abstention, and that fairness evaluation should consider biased responses, abstention, prompt formulation, and answer-option design jointly.

title: Joint Semantic-Channel Coding and Modulation for Generative Image Transmission
authors: Hao Cao, Jingkai Ying, Yinhuan Huang, Zhijin Qin, Yuan Shen
abstract: Digital image transmission typically optimizes source coding, channel coding, and modulation separately, limiting how source representations adapt to channel impairments. We propose SemQAM, a joint semantic-channel coding and modulation scheme for generative image transmission converting source to modulated symbols, such as standard QAM symbols. Channel impairments create two challenges: they can corrupt the latent representation at the receiver, and this corruption can compound through autoregressive coding, degrading reconstruction quality. First, SemQAM represents latent features with vector quantization (VQ), maps each VQ index to a QAM symbol, and updates the codeword corresponding to the detected symbol so that channel impairments directly affect codebook learning. Moreover, SemQAM uses the conditional expectation of received codewords to approximate the receiver reconstruction and reduce error propagation during autoregressive coding. SemQAM supports multiple SNRs and CBRs in a unified model, while also supporting conventional source coding through SemQAM-C. Experiments show that (i) under the same LDPC and QAM settings, SemQAM-C outperforms OneDC in LPIPS and DISTS with substantially lower complexity, showing that the unified model retains competitive capability for source coding. (ii) Compared with this separated counterpart, SemQAM reduces channel uses by 18.57% at matched LPIPS and outperforms the compared JSCC methods, demonstrating the benefit of joint coding.

title: Cross-Area Transfer Learning for VLC-based Indoor Localization with a Transfer Efficiency Score
authors: Masood Jan, Wafa Njima, Xun Zhang, Alexander Artemenko
abstract: Indoor localization systems are critical for Industry-4.0 applications. Visible Light Communication (VLC)-based systems offer advantages such as immunity to electromagnetic interference, high accuracy, and energy efficiency, but their performance is hindered by environmental variability across deployment areas. This paper presents a transfer learning (TL) framework for VLC-based indoor localization that enhances cross-area robustness while reducing data requirements. Using real-world measurements from four distinct areas of a Bosch manufacturing facility, we show that fine-tuning a deep neural network (DNN) pre-trained on source area data with only 40% of target-area measurements recovers 97% of full-data performance, thereby reducing the amount of target data needed. We further introduce the Transfer Efficiency Score (TES), a composite metric that identifies the most effective source models for transfer without exhaustive evaluation. Guided by TES, the framework selects the best source model, yielding localization errors as low as 40.9 cm with success rates above 86%. Validation on an unseen area confirms its generalization capability, with a 3.28 cm mean error achieved using the TES-selected source model. Overall, the proposed framework provides a scalable and data-efficient pathway for industrial VLC localization, substantially reducing deployment costs and computational burden while maintaining high accuracy in diverse and dynamic environments.

title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
authors: Joydeep Chakravarty, Yoav Zigdon
abstract: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. Solving wave equations of bulk fields with different spins outside the black brane, we calculate exponentially small contributions to retarded Green's functions in the dual CFT at large real frequency. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of paths in an analytically continued classical black brane interior via a WKB approximation: they provide the complex time elapsed along null geodesics that reflect off the singularity, and incorporate the corresponding reflection coefficients.

title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
authors: Zhennan Wan, Jianfei Chen
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose $\textbf{LongZero}$, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs.

title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
authors: Tianyu Liang, Chao Chen, James Demmel, Yang Liu
abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Matérn system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.

title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
authors: Ji-seong Chae
abstract: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. We analytically continue the gravitational amplitudes computed from these triangulations to de Sitter parameters and use them to infer OPE correlations. We recover matching normalized amplitudes from a complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction. A non-Gaussian fourth moment encodes the hyperbolic core volume in an oscillatory semiclassical phase. We construct the associated Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime and show that derivatives of this phase recover its boost holonomies. Its spacelike future boundary carries a positive-definite conformal metric, while the wavefunction obeys Euclidean conformal Ward identities. These relations connect the proposed OPE statistics to both the Euclidean boundary description and the Lorentzian bulk geometry. Integrating the absolute square of the cosmological wavefunction over boundary moduli gives cosmological observables. Their long-collar factorization reproduces the edge measure of the two-matrix model.

title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
authors: Sunjun Hwang, Lee Wei Wesley Wong, Liang Jie Wong, Leong Chuan Kwek
abstract: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.

title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
authors: Houde Qian, Zheng Jiang, Wenyi Li, Chenxi Xu, Xinjie Lin, Yuzhao Peng, Ruoyu Han, Youjie Zheng, Kaisen Yang, Qinhuai Na, You Fu, Calvin Xiao
abstract: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period. We introduce Quant-Arena, a benchmark and public leaderboard for end-to-end quantitative research on real A-share market data. A model constructs features and stock-scoring code, receives feedback only on 2022--2023, and freezes one strategy for assessment on the sealed year 2024. A cash-account evaluator applies trading constraints and costs, including market impact estimated from a simulated order book. Scores are dominated by realized excess return and complemented by signal quality and the diversity of features used by the strategy. We evaluate nine frontier models, among which GPT-6 Astra scores highest; yet no model beats the equal-weight market in 2024. Quant-Arena is open to submissions from any model or agent harness.

title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
authors: Yanzhe Chen, Ziyi Yang, Jifeng Zhu, Qiming Huang, Ruihe An, Peiyao Xu, Hesen Yang, Runda Liu, Chang Gong, Zhijun Cao, Zechen Bai, Wenzheng Zeng, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Mike Zheng Shou
abstract: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the current state, Anticipate action effects, Plan a feasible course, Act through an interface or body, and Verify the outcome. Defined by function rather than architecture, these capabilities let PAPAV identify what all three share and then compare MMEAs with MMAs and with RSs.
